units.text: INT. DOLLHOUSE - CONTINUOUS
I have it in me to become a different man.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Perhaps—if your doll is taken away from you.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But to part!—to part from you! No, no, Nora, I can’t understand that idea.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: going out to the right.
. That makes it all the more certain that it must be done.
units.name: NORA

units.text: She comes back with her cloak and hat and a small bag which she puts on a chair by the table.
Nora, Nora, not now! Wait until tomorrow.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: putting on her cloak.
. I cannot spend the night in a strange man’s room.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But can’t we live here like brother and sister—?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: putting on her hat.
. You know very well that would not last long.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Puts the shawl round her.
Goodbye, Torvald. I won’t see the little ones. I know they are in better hands than mine. As I am now, I can be of no use to them.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But some day, Nora—some day?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: How can I tell? I have no idea what is going to become of me.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But you are my wife, whatever becomes of you.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Listen, Torvald. I have heard that when a wife deserts her husband’s house, as I am doing now, he is legally freed from all obligations towards her. In any case, I set you free from all your obligations. You are not to feel yourself bound in the slightest way, any more than I shall. There must be perfect freedom on both sides. See, here is your ring back. Give me mine.
units.name: NORA

units.text: That too?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: That too.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Here it is.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: That’s right. Now it is all over. I have put the keys here. The maids know all about everything in the house—better than I do. Tomorrow, after I have left her, Christine will come here and pack up my own things that I brought with me from home. I will have them sent after me.
units.name: NORA

units.text: All over! All over!—Nora, shall you never think of me again?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: I know I shall often think of you, the children, and this house.
units.name: NORA

units.text: May I write to you, Nora?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: No—never. You must not do that.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But at least let me send you—
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Nothing—nothing—
units.name: NORA

units.text: Let me help you if you are in want.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: No. I can receive nothing from a stranger.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Nora—can I never be anything more than a stranger to you?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: taking her bag.
. Ah, Torvald, the most wonderful thing of all would have to happen.
units.name: NORA

units.text: Tell me what that would be!
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Both you and I would have to be so changed that—. Oh, Torvald, I don’t believe any longer in wonderful things happening.
units.name: NORA

units.text: But I will believe in it. Tell me! So changed that—?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: That our life together would be a real wedlock. Goodbye.
units.name: NORA

units.text: She goes out through the hall.
sinks down on a chair at the door and buries his face in his hands.
. Nora! Nora!
units.name: HELMER

units.text: Looks round, and rises.
Empty. She is gone.
units.name: HELMER

units.text: A hope flashes across his mind.
The most wonderful thing of all—?
units.name: HELMER

units.text: The sound of a door shutting is heard from below.
